findings.text: Upheld (Q2 logic duplicated and diverged; Q6 behaviour). `listProjects` decides `remote` with `alias LIKE 'remote:%'`, a second copy of the rule that `isHostLedAlias` (src/sharing/levels.ts:25) applies in `setLevel` (src/sharing/store.ts:338) and `entryAliases` (src/sharing/report.ts:182,191). I checked this against the code. For a project whose only remote is a local path or a `file://` origin, the dock enables the level control and hides the no-remote sentence, and the PUT then answers 409 `no-remote`, which the person sees only as 'The level could not be saved.' The doc comment at src/ui/api.ts:61 ('which a level is bound to') is false for such a remote. Fix: compute `remote` through `isHostLedAlias`.

Upheld (Q2, logic duplicated, not a line of boilerplate). `counterIn` decodes the epoch with a hard-coded `2 ** 20`. That restates the layout that `epochOf` builds from the private `HASH_BITS = 20` (src/sharing/levels.ts:89,108). This is the encoding rule written twice: a change to `HASH_BITS` would make `withChange` compute wrong preview epochs, and nothing would say so. Fix: export the constant or a decoder from levels.ts.
Advisory (Q10/Q6): the 'destinations' doc block sits above the `REMOTE_ALIAS` comment, so `DESTINATIONS` (line 14) has no doc block and `REMOTE_ALIAS` has two.

Advisory (Q5/Q8): `policyWith`, `resetSharingLog` and the re-export of `GENERATION_KEY`/`newGeneration` in store.ts:25 are test-only exports from production modules. The rubric files an unused or test-only export as advisory.

Advisory (Q2, duplicated boilerplate): the two sharing key names are declared again in store.ts, patch.ts, share.ts (`LIST_KEYS`) and status/report.ts (`SHARING_LISTS`), while settings.ts already exports `SHARING_KEYS`.
Advisory (Q2, one line): `rootOf` repeats the scope-to-root expression that `entryRefusal` writes inline in policy.ts.

Advisory (Q9): the `hasTable` guards in `knowledgeReadable` and `readStore` work around `moduleSchemaState` answering `current` when there is no `module_migrations` table. The workaround is documented and the reviewer filed it as advisory.

Advisory (Q2): `save()` re-derives 'widens' against the lists in force, while the server's `previewSettingsPatch` decides it against the file's lists. The server still refuses the same writes, so no behaviour breaks today.
Advisory (Q2): `SharingReport`, `SharingChange`, `SharingView` and `PolicyChange` restate the server's types by hand. Type-only imports would avoid drift.
Advisory (Q5): `sharingStatus` parses the env file a second time through `publicSettings`, right after `loadPolicy` has parsed it.
Advisory (Q5): `confirm` is now a layer that only forwards to `askYesNo(question, true)`.

Advisory (Q11). This is new prose, so no old fact is dropped. Still, 'needs a git remote' is wider than the enforced rule, which refuses a remote that is a local path or a `file://` origin. Align it with ADR 0025.

Lowered to advisory: this names a line of the item's evidence record, not a line of the diff, so under the judge's rule it cannot hold the gate. The substance holds against rubric Q4. The recorded reason for AC-18 says the docs are 'prose with no behaviour a test could fail on before they exist'. Yet the same record says probes/check-docs.ts fails when any named part is missing, so a red run on the tree before round two's text was possible, and only the green run (exit 0) is recorded. The session should record a red run or correct the reason.

Advisory, as filed. The test matches spec.md:333, which keeps an entry by hash alone whatever the versions. The recorded text in criteria-round-two.md differs, and spec.md:346 records that the author's decision on it is pending. AC-5 is read through the spec line in force.

Advisory: this names a probe outside the diff. The clause 'its other assertions unchanged' for tests/unit/module-migrations.test.ts is not compared with part 1's version. The new case does have a red run under AC-1.
Advisory: AC-21's 'hash only candidates with a ledger record' is proven on the helpers, as the criterion allows. No test of `wouldLeave` would fail if `leavingMemories` hashed every candidate.
Advisory (Q5): the guard checks for the literal `error.message`, so other spellings would pass it. Reverting the code that was actually changed still fails the test.
Advisory: install.ts's `confirm` is covered only through unit tests of `askYesNo(…, true)`. No test goes through install itself.
Advisory (Q6): the test does not assert that the detail names `WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_SHARE_AREAS`.

Advisory, as filed. `OutgoingEntry.frontmatter` carries the `author` name, and ADR 0025 does not name it among what leaves. Nothing is sent in this part. Before part 6 sends anything, the ADR should state that the author leaves, or the payload should pin the frontmatter fields that may leave.

Advisory (the reviewer cited diff.patch line 9895, which is `validatePatch` here). `validatePatch` refuses `\r`/`\n`, which closes the round-one injection. Refusing every other C0 control character would be hardening beyond the risk areas.

Advisory (the reviewer cited diff.patch line 13110). `GET /api/sharing` writes: it reconciles, logs and refreshes git. It sits behind the same Host and token checks as every route, so no new caller reaches it.
Advisory: the projects line keeps the plural for one project ('1 projects share knowledge'), seen in review/ui/settings-sharing-problems@1512.png.

Advisory: the problems alert shows developer-voiced strings that start in lower case, name an env variable and are joined by '·', and its second part repeats the inert-area row (review/ui/settings-sharing-problems@1512.png). This is not a raw error, so it is not a defect under Q5.

Advisory: in the locked state, '1 entry would leave' sits next to an off switch with no sentence explaining it (review/ui/settings-sharing-locked@1512.png). The manifest's observation gives the cause.
Advisory (Q11): the suffix 'in the area' is repeated on every area row. The page still passes the squint test.

Kept as advisory. review/ui/console-settings-sharing-error.json logs the browser's 'Failed to load resource … 500' for the write failure that the declared error state induces (a read-only data directory). The page's code produces no error, and the toast shows only the plain sentence. No review/ui-evidence.json lists this file, so it cannot carry a ui-ux defect in any case. On the reviewer's Not answerable items: the nine stale captures were retaken on the code under review (manifest roundTwo.retaken). Loading and saving are transient states under a second, which the rubric files as advisory. The manifest has no summary.missing, the plan names no viewports and the thesis names no interactions, so no defect falls at the capture spec.

Advisory, as filed. The rollback is stated, but its 'levels are Nothing after a restored copy' does not hold for a v7 backup restored under 0.6.0. 0.6.0 has no `resetLevels`, so on re-upgrade the copy's levels, its counter and its generation take force with no `restore` row. Nothing leaves in this part. The ADR and the spec should name this path before parts 5 and 6 rely on the epoch and the generation.

Upheld (Q1 and Q3). `ProjectSummary.remote` is computed at the edge with its own SQL test, `alias LIKE 'remote:%'`. ADR 0025 § Identity and the field's own doc comment (src/ui/api.ts:61) bind a level only to a host-led alias (`isHostLedAlias`, which `setLevel` and `entryAliases` apply). So the route's field means something other than the domain rule it documents. For a project whose only remote is a path or `file://`, the dock enables a control that the server then refuses with 409 `no-remote`. Fix: derive `remote` through `isHostLedAlias`, and pin it with a case in tests/integration/ui-sharing.test.ts.

Advisory (Q6): policy.ts imports read helpers from store.ts, against the Design's 'neither imports the other'. There is no cycle and no boundary is crossed. Record the direction, or move the helpers into a leaf.
Advisory: `areasOf` is a second, non-throwing reader of the knowledge taxonomy beside `taxonomyFor`. The fail-closed reading is what the Design wants.

Advisory: the viewer decides 'widens' against the lists in force rather than through `previewSettingsPatch`. The server refuses all the same, so this is a Design detail read differently, with no boundary crossed.
Advisory (Q2): the OR on `direction` keeps the primary key from serving `ledgerRecords`, so the query scans the whole ledger. The table has no writer yet, and the ADR states the single scan.
Advisory (Q2): the `(?n IS NULL OR …)` predicates in `findEntry` keep it from using `UNIQUE (repo_id, slug)`. This makes a slower lookup, not a defect.

Advisory. probes/restore-journal-mode.md answers the reviewer's open Q6: the `VACUUM INTO` copy is already in rollback-journal mode before this PRAGMA, and a restore without this item leaves the store in that mode too. So the item does not newly drop WAL. The underlying gap in `openDb` (src/store/db.ts:177) is pre-existing debt, already made its own item.
Advisory (Q4): the `\n`-joined title and body can collide, and the hash depends on the calling process's redaction environment. Settle the encoding before part 6 writes any ledger row.
Advisory (Q5): no retention or erasure is stated for `sharing_ledger` and `sharing_changes`. This part writes no ledger row, so part 5 or 6 must state the retention before it writes one.
